image_description: A male mallard duck (drake) standing on a grassy bank near water. The duck features the characteristic iridescent green head, white neck ring, chestnut breast, and grey body. Its yellow bill is clearly visible, as are its orange webbed feet. The background consists of blurred dry branches and water.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Most distinctive feature is the broad, flat bill adapted for filter-feeding; bill is dark grey to yellow-green.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bill is clearly visible, broad, flat, and yellow-green in color, matching the description perfectly.
The eye is visible and appears dark/black, consistent with the taxonomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is stocky and compact, streamlined and buoyant with dense waterproof plumage.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The body shape is robust and streamlined. The plumage appears dense and smooth, indicative of waterproof feathers.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Breeding plumage is typically more colorful than female: common patterns include iridescent green head with white neck ring and grey body (mallard), or chestnut head with grey body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image shows the classic mallard drake pattern: iridescent green head, distinct white neck ring, chestnut breast, and grey flanks.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Legs are short and set far back on the body with webbed feet (three forward toes connected by webbing).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The legs are orange, positioned towards the rear of the body. The visible foot shows clear webbing between the toes.
The folded wing is visible on the side, appearing broad and tapering to a point at the tail end.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is short with curled central tail feathers (drake feathers) in many species.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is short, and the characteristic upward curl of the central tail feathers (drake feathers) is clearly visible at the rear.
